create.name: James Baraz
create.bio:
James Baraz has taught insight meditation since 1978 and helped found Spirit Rock, the Marin County meditation centre, as one of its first teachers. Before meditation became his work he spent twelve years as a primary school teacher, and that ease with explaining things plainly shows in how he teaches. He is the guiding teacher of the Insight Meditation Community of Berkeley, which meets every Thursday evening at the Berkeley Buddhist Monastery and on Zoom, and he advises One Earth Sangha, an online community exploring Buddhist responses to the climate crisis.

He is best known for Awakening Joy, an online course he has run each year since 2003 that takes the Buddhist teachings on wholesome states and turns them into ten monthly themes, from gratitude and integrity to letting go and compassion. More than twenty thousand people in some thirty countries have taken it, and a teacher training lets graduates lead it themselves. With Shoshana Alexander he wrote a book of the same name, and with the teacher Michele Lilyanna a companion guide for parents and educators. He leads silent retreats at Spirit Rock and the Insight Meditation Society, and weekend workshops at Esalen, recently with his son Adam. He lives in Berkeley with his wife, Jane.

books.title: Awakening Joy: 10 Steps to True Happiness
books.author: James Baraz, Shoshana Alexander
books.description: The book version of his long-running course, written with Shoshana Alexander, with a foreword by Jack Kornfield and a preface by Ram Dass. Ten chapters each take one theme, such as gratitude or letting go, and pair stories with practices to try. This is the Parallax Press edition; it first came out from Bantam in 2010.

books.title: Awakening Joy for Kids: A Hands-On Guide for Grown-Ups to Nourish Themselves and Raise Mindful, Happy Children
books.author: James Baraz, Michele Lilyanna
books.description: Written with the primary school teacher Michele Lilyanna for parents and teachers. It adapts the ten Awakening Joy themes into activities and conversations for children, while asking adults to do the practices themselves first.

courses.title: Embodying Joy: Relaxing the Body Into Being
courses.description: A weekend at Esalen led with his son Adam Baraz, moving through five phases named after the elements, from water to space. Guided meditation, gentle movement, partner exercises and reflection draw on Buddhist practice and Adam's body-based approach.

courses.title: 2027 Awakening Joy Course
courses.description: A five-month online course of ten live Zoom sessions held every other Tuesday, each built around one theme with a guided meditation and a practice letter. Recordings stay available until the end of 2027, and students can join after it starts.

courses.title: Awakening Joy Teacher Training
courses.description: A training that runs alongside the annual course for people who want to lead Awakening Joy groups themselves. Details and the application sit in a free module on the course site.

free_resources.title: James Baraz's Dharma talks on Dharma Seed
free_resources.description: A large free archive of his recorded talks and guided meditations from Spirit Rock and other retreat centres. A good way to hear how he teaches insight and lovingkindness practice.

free_resources.title: 18-Minute Guided Mindfulness Meditation
free_resources.description: A short guided sitting he recorded, free to stream or download as an MP3. The same page links his printed meditation instructions and an exploration of the RAIN practice.

free_resources.title: Conversations with the Wise
free_resources.description: Free recorded conversations in which he talks with teachers and writers such as Tara Brach, Jack Kornfield and Rick Hanson about practising through hard times.

free_resources.title: Insight Meditation Community of Berkeley weekly sitting
free_resources.description: His Thursday evening meditation group with a dharma talk and discussion, held at the Berkeley Buddhist Monastery and on Zoom. Open to all and supported by donation.
